title: `Core\Regex::matches` allocates twice on every call, even on a cached pattern.
text: `benches/members/core/Regex/matches.nvs` counts about 2 allocations a call against a declared `allocations 0`, for a member that returns a `bool` from a pattern already in the compile cache. The member's own path on a cache hit reads borrowed data only: `pattern_of` reads the `Pattern`'s slots, `text` borrows the string and the cache lookup clones an `Rc`. Not checked: whether the two come from `step_budget`, which reads the request configuration on every call, from the linear engine's per-search state, or from the call boundary for a `Pattern|string` parameter. Closing it starts with finding which one, and `matches`'s bench then declares the count it reaches.
